status: DESIGN APPENDIX v3 (backlog): rows for milestones M3-M5 and 'post'. Not loaded by the game and not gated by the data test; a row moves into the live file, and under test, when its milestone starts. Rows may reference live ids.
summary: The other regions, off-map nodes, routes, travel modes and encounters; the fort region's other eras.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

setting.default: New York: the upper Mohawk valley, the Oneida Carry, Oriska and the Oneida country, with Albany off-map (M5). The live slice is one region (map_regions.json).
setting.structure: Playable regions of about 1-1.5 km, each its own Godot scene, joined by a painted travel map.

institutions.rule: Each region names one institutions block; the economy, land, fish and trade systems read it (review 1, blocker). The default frame is New York.

how: lease from a patentee or manor (service.patent_lease)
land_regime.title_rests_on: Crown patents resting on Indian deeds; some deeds were fraudulent and are disputed (seasons.json event.deed_dispute: the Kayaderosseras patent, the Canajoharie and George Klock disputes)
land_regime.squatting: marking a lot without a lease or deed gives no right; tomahawk and cabin rights do not apply

new_york.trade_regulator: seasons.json trade_regulators by era; Johnson's Northern Department (Indian Department) and its commissaries

pennsylvania_ohio.trade_regulator: the Pennsylvania commissioners' store at Fort Pitt (1759-64), then the Plan of 1764, then colonial regulation
pennsylvania_ohio.note: Used only by the Ohio node, or if the default setting moves to the Susquehanna or the upper Ohio.

travel_map.shows: known routes, estimate with season and danger, reported dangers, closures
travel_map.camps: needs.json time_safety.travel (stop at dusk, camp roll from kit and Survival, departure warning, drop in to camp by hand)
travel_map.encounter_scenes: small generated scenes whose terrain follows the route kind
travel_map.loading: next region loads in the background (ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request)

patent_leased_or_bought.claims: a lot needs a lease or a deed from the patentee; rent or the purchase balance falls due

nation_town_lands.note: the town, its fields, orchards and pastures

nation_hunting_grounds.claims: dispute: -25 standing with the nation and town, -10 colonial authorities after 1763
nation_hunting_grounds.hunting: by the town's leave: ask the hunters' fall camp or the council (social.ask_leave), or have the interpreter or the post trader broker it; without leave -2 standing per carcass
nation_hunting_grounds.note: unceded land; encroachment was a root cause of war (E:9.7, E:S33); colonial hunters on Iroquois grounds after the 1763 Proclamation were a standing Oneida complaint to Johnson (N:21)

contested.claims: no; a war zone in war eras
contested.note: patrols and armed parties in war years

beyond_line.claims: illegal beyond the Fort Stanwix line: -15 colonial authorities, -25 with the nation

patent_claimed_disputed_carry.claims: not allowed without the patentee's deed; the Oneida dispute the claim
patent_claimed_disputed_carry.note: The Carry: colonists claimed it under the Oriskany patent (1705); the Roof family bought land beside the fort from Oliver De Lancey, who held the easternmost part of that patent (N:1). The Oneida disputed the patent, and the 1768 line began here (review 1 of v2, minor 9).

resource_nodes.note: elm, birch, basswood; season gate bark_peel

trap_night_density_prime.note: Base nightly catch weight per species for one well-placed trap in good habitat (actions.json trap_model). Region multipliers below; month activity in activity_by_month.

beaver.note: under ice: lodge hunts and ice-hole sets

hunt_spawns_per_region_season.unit: animal groups present in the loaded region; respawn after explicit game days (no process rule)

default.note: the town's own grounds: hunt by leave

species_notes.elk: Eastern elk lived across Pennsylvania and New York in the 18th century (K:22).
species_notes.bison: The eastern population of the plains bison (Bison bison) reached western Pennsylvania and the Ohio Country; not the northwestern wood bison. Not in the starting regions (K:22).
species_notes.moose: Moose lived in the Adirondack and lake country and were taken on the late-winter snow crust (K:2).
species_notes.cougar: Rare but present in the 1760s Northeast.

regions.name: The Oneida Carry
regions.drainage: watershed: Mohawk (east) and Wood Creek to Oneida Lake (west)
regions.modelled_on: the Oneida Carry between the Mohawk and Wood Creek (N:1, N:2)

era_states.era.war_1755_1758: 1755 to March 1756: Forts Williams and Bull and a magazine; Fort Bull destroyed 27 March 1756; rebuilt works that summer; Webb destroys every work on 31 August 1756 and falls back to German Flatts; the Carry lies abandoned (patrols, Oneida carriers) until Fort Stanwix is begun on 26 August 1758. No post and no tariff board.
era_states.era.war_1759_1760: Fort Stanwix garrisoned; sutlers, bateau men, Oneida carriers; the Roof family's inn and hauling from 1759. A military zone.
era_states.era.tense_peace_1761_1762: a small garrison; traders by the commander's leave; posted 1761 tariffs
era_states.era.war_1763_1764: a garrison on alert; trade thin
era_states.era.peace_1765_1767: a trader's store at the landing by the commissary's leave; Roof's inn; Oriska east of the Carry; the tariffs Johnson applied administratively
era_states.era.line_1768_1773: the congress of October-November 1768 camps here; the new line begins at the Carry; the fort decays; trade unregulated

pois.note: the Roof (Rueff) family's inn and hauling (N:1)
Forts Williams and Bull (1755-56); Fort Stanwix (from August 1758)

Oriska, east of the Carry: grew up in the 1760s where Oneida and settler households met; of about 90 residents only half were Oneida; villagers sold food, hauled goods and traded with travellers (N:1). Settlers' stock in the corn is a dispute here.

era_states.era.peace_1765_1767: growth: new leases and purchases, potash kettles, a mill
era_states.era.line_1768_1773: settler pressure west toward the line; deed disputes

era_states.era.war_1759_1760: Amherst takes Ticonderoga and Crown Point (1759); the front moves north; supply convoys on the road from Albany and Fort Edward
era_states.era.peace_1765_1767: abandoned works, discharged soldiers' land grants, hunters
era_states.era.line_1768_1773: grants and settlement creep north from Fort Edward

foot.notes: listed hours are foot hours on the route

wagon.closed: mud season and deep snow on the Albany road (seasons.json gates)

bateau.note: The bateau (battoe) carried freight on the Mohawk-Wood Creek route in the 1750s-60s; the Schenectady or Durham-type boat came into common use in the 1790s. Whole bateaux crossed the Carry on wagons or sledges or on carriers' shoulders (review 1 of v2, minor 7).
bateau.portage: wagons, sledges or carriers haul the whole boat across the Carry

routes.note: M5: from the manor woods west past the Carry to the Oneida hunting grounds
Wood Creek, Oneida Lake and the Oswego River
Albany to Fort Edward to Lake George, the military road; about as far as Albany is from German Flatts

encounters.chance_per_game_hour: 0.04 * route.danger * season_mult * war_mult * mode_mult * cargo_mult * (1 - 0.3 * max(survival, hunting)/100)
encounters.cargo_mult: 1 + carried trade value / 2,880 d, max 2 (routes with danger_scales_with_cargo)

enc.settled.effect: a nation's trading party on the road: trade, news (mkt.native_trading_party)
help: standing +3, costs time and food
wet goods or lame horse (load security matters)

enc.wilderness.effect: deer, bear, turkey or wolves by season
news, trade, a share of game
upset canoe or bateau: goods and powder wet; fall through ice in a thaw
+2 game hours unless a Survival check at difficulty 30

enc.contested.rule: friend or foe by the war state and the alignment of the party's named community (npcs.json alignments); avoidable with a hunting or survival check

enc.contested.note: ranging companies were disbanded after the war; in 1765 a patrol is a hired scout or an express

enc.contested.effect: a burned farm: report the loss at the fort or valley (standing +3), bury the dead (time), or help survivors to safety (food and time; standing +5). Nothing to loot (review 1, issue 21).
families fleeing raids: share food, escort them, or pass by
enc.contested.note: In this corridor refugees belong to 1755-58 (German Flatts, November 1757 and April 1758; the lake country). 1763 and 1774 refugee flows were on the Pennsylvania and Virginia frontiers (node.west).

era_states.era.war_1755_1758: no post yet: the ford on the carrying road; provincial and regular parties pass; the German Flatts raid (November 1757) sends refugees down the valley; the post is built in 1758
era_states.era.war_1759_1760: a supply post for the Oswego and Niagara campaigns: provincials, rangers, bateau men and wagon traffic; army hiring and meat contracts
era_states.era.tense_peace_1761_1762: a small garrison after the conquest; Amherst's economies; ranging companies disbanded; the post shrinks
era_states.era.war_1763_1764: on alert through Pontiac's War; New York provincials pass with Bradstreet in 1764
era_states.era.line_1768_1773: given up: a caretaker or no one; the buildings decay; the 1768 congress passes up the river to the Carry
